note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparisons with A. aneristus, A. apocnetus and A. hilarus have been made. The alate of A. pacatus is notable for its large compound eyes and ocelli. Its worker differs in the very slender fore tibia, the shorter mandibular apical tooth and the bilobed, dorsally placed enteric valve seat. In A. prosenus the apical teeth are longer in both castes, the worker fore tibia is more slender, and the neck of the enteric valve seat is shorter. No sign of abdominal dehiscence was observed in the few worker specimens available.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white; pilosity very sparse, pale yellow and inconspicuous; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.30, Pcl/Rj 2.45. Mandibular apical tooth rather short, La/Li 0.66, Ra/Ri 0.85; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/Li·Lm 9.95; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth about equal in length, Ra/Ry·Rm 12.85. Fore tibia scarcely thickened, Ti/Tw 4.96; third apical spur small but clearly present, not reduced. The midgut–hindgut overlap is oblique and lies to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot; in the unopened abdomen the enteric valve seat is ventral, with three distinct lobes, the third slightly smaller, and joined to the second hindgut pouch by a very long neck; the valve membrane bears minute spines outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle slightly smaller than the ocellus, circular, flat, pale yellowish brown; central spot circular, less than half the fontanelle, slightly raised, brown; postclypeus brown, labrum yellow; frontal groove distinct, flat, semicircular, brown; antennae very pale yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum brown, the dark transverse sutures present but indistinct; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellowish white. Abdominal tergites pale brown, dorsal spiracles paler, sternites yellowish brown, ventral spiracles pale; cerci yellowish white. Posterior margin of head capsule not very evenly rounded, slightly undulate behind the eyes; ocelli moderate, their distance from the compound eye about equal to their minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.26, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture present. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.59, Ra/Ri 0.76; a distinct notch, in surface view, separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence, La/Li·Lm 7.53; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are roughly aligned, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth nearly equal. Meso- and metanotum moderately broad at the constriction, M/W 0.30. Cephalic pilosity pale brown, rather even, almost forming a layer, with longer outstanding setae.
